title: Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu et sur les machines propres à développer cette puissance
author: Sadi Carnot
notes: Original memoir on the motive power of heat. Introduced the reversible cycle and efficiency bound η = 1 - T_c/T_h. Foundational work; English translations available.

title: On the Calorific Effects of Magneto-Electricity, and on the Mechanical Value of Heat
author: James Prescott Joule
notes: Experimental demonstration of mechanical-to-thermal energy conversion. Established first law foundation: ΔU = Q - W. Refuted caloric theory.

title: Ueber die bewegende Kraft der Wärme und die Gesetze, welche sich daraus für die Wärmenlehre selbst ableiten lassen
author: Rudolf Clausius
notes: Formalized the second law and introduced entropy. Key statement: ΔS ≥ dQ_rev/T for all processes. Clausius inequality is central to modern thermodynamics.

title: Weitere Studien über das Wärmegleichgewicht unter Gasmolekülen
author: Ludwig Boltzmann
notes: Breakthrough: S = k_B ln Ω. Connected macroscopic entropy to number of accessible microstates. Laid foundation for statistical mechanics interpretation of thermodynamics.

title: On the Equilibrium of Heterogeneous Substances
author: Josiah Willard Gibbs
notes: Unified thermodynamic potentials (U, H, F, G). Introduced Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies. Fundamental to chemistry, phase equilibria, and equilibrium theory.

title: Treatise on Thermodynamics (3rd ed.)
author: Max Planck
notes: Synthesis of classical thermodynamics with statistical mechanics and early quantum theory. Planck's statement of the third law. Bridge to modern quantum thermodynamics.

title: Thermodynamics and an Introduction to Thermostatistics (2nd ed.)
author: Herbert B. Callen
notes: Canonical modern reference for rigorous classical thermodynamics. Postulational approach; entropy as fundamental. Derives all major relations from first principles. Advanced undergraduate to graduate.

title: Fundamentals of Statistical and Thermal Physics
author: Frederick Reif
notes: Bridges macroscopic thermodynamics and statistical mechanics pedagogically. Clear treatment of ensembles, partition functions, emergence of thermodynamics. Intermediate to advanced undergraduate. Excellent worked examples.

title: Thermal Physics (2nd ed.)
author: Charles Kittel & Herbert Kroemer
notes: Elegant treatment of statistical mechanics and thermodynamics with modern applications. Partition functions, density of states, Debye model, Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics. Advanced undergraduate to graduate.

title: An Introduction to Thermal Physics
author: Daniel V. Schroeder
notes: Modern undergraduate text integrating classical and statistical thermodynamics. Clear figures, intuitive explanations, computer simulations. Widely used in US universities. Excellent pedagogical clarity.

title: Heat and Thermodynamics (7th ed.)
author: Mark W. Zemansky & Richard H. Dittman
notes: Classic engineering and physics text with historical commentary. Thorough treatment of first and second laws, cycles, real gases. Intermediate to advanced undergraduate. Extensive problem sets.

title: The Fluctuation Theorem
author: Denis J. Evans & Debra J. Searles
notes: Modern breakthrough in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. Fluctuation theorem connects time-reversal symmetry violations to entropy production far from equilibrium. Advanced research-level.

title: Nonequilibrium Equality for Free Energy Differences
author: Christopher Jarzynski
notes: Jarzynski equality: exp(-β ΔF) = ⟨exp(-β W)⟩. Landmark result; enables measurement of free energies via non-equilibrium pulling. Foundation for molecular dynamics and single-molecule experiments.

title: Entropy Production Fluctuation Theorem and the Second Law
author: Gavin E. Crooks
notes: Crooks fluctuation theorem: P(W) / P(-W_reverse) = exp(β W). Deepens understanding of irreversibility and microscopic reversibility. Advanced research-level.

title: Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process
author: Rolf Landauer
notes: Landauer's principle: erasing one bit of information dissipates ≥ k_B T ln 2 of heat. Connects information and thermodynamics. Foundational to quantum computing and computation thermodynamics.

title: Demons, Engines, and the Second Law
author: Charles H. Bennett
notes: Beautifully written essay resolving Maxwell's demon paradox. Shows why local entropy decrease requires observer entropy increase via information storage/erasure. Undergraduate to advanced. Highly recommended for conceptual clarity.

title: Molecular Biology of the Cell: An Evolutionary Perspective
author: Lukas Kovac
notes: Thermodynamics in living systems. How cells maintain low-entropy order against second law via energy consumption. Coupling of exergonic/endergonic reactions via ΔG. Modern biology needs thermodynamic thinking.

title: Statistical Mechanics (2nd ed.)
author: Kerson Huang
notes: Comprehensive graduate-level treatment of classical and quantum statistical mechanics. Derivation of thermodynamics from first principles, phase transitions, critical phenomena. Renormalization group approach.

title: Statistical Mechanics (3rd ed.)
author: Rajendra K. Pathria & Paul D. Beale
notes: Modern graduate text. Rigorous treatment of ensembles, Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics, phase transitions, critical phenomena. Extensive problems and appendices. Standard in graduate programs.

title: Biological Physics: Energy, Information, Life
author: Philip Nelson
notes: Thermodynamics and statistical mechanics applied to biology: protein folding, membranes, molecular motors. Bridges physics and molecular biology with clarity. Real examples and order-of-magnitude estimates.

title: Introduction to Thermodynamics of Irreversible Processes
author: Ilya Prigogine
notes: Foundational work on non-equilibrium thermodynamics. Entropy production, phenomenological coefficients (Onsager relations), minimum entropy production principle. Dissipative structures and self-organization.

title: A Gallavotti–Cohen-type Symmetry Related to Cycle Decompositions for Markov Chains and Biochemical Applications
author: Joel L. Lebowitz & Herbert Spohn
notes: Modern extension of fluctuation theorems to stochastic processes and biochemical cycles. Explains directed motion of molecular machines (kinesin, ATPase) despite thermal noise. Advanced research-level.

title: A Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism (Vol. 1-2)
author: James Clerk Maxwell
notes: Introduced the thought experiment of Maxwell's demon (1867). Poses a challenge to the second law: can a being sorting fast/slow molecules decrease entropy? Resolved by Bennett via information theory.

title: Stochastic Processes in Physics and Chemistry (3rd ed.)
author: N. G. Van Kampen
notes: Comprehensive treatment of stochastic processes underlying statistical mechanics. Langevin equations, Fokker-Planck equations, noise. Essential for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and molecular dynamics.

title: Searching for Simplicity: The Progress of Thermodynamics
author: Denis J. Evans (ed.)
notes: Historical and philosophical review of thermodynamics. Evolution from phenomenological to statistical foundations. Discusses open problems and future directions in non-equilibrium theory.
